newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank profits up, U.S. unit helps.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank profits up, U.S. unit helps.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland said Wednesday a strong performance from its British banking operations helped fuel a 23 percent increase in first-half profits.
The bank said its pre-tax profits for the six months ended March 31 rose to 369 million pounds ($603 million) from 301 million pounds the previous year.

Chief Executive George Mathewson said a 24 percent increase in pretax earnings, market penetration on the corporate side, good growth in retail savings and "excellent credit card performance" made for "a very satisfactory outcome."

Royal Bank's U.S. retail banking arm, Citizens, had performed well following its successful acquisition of First New Hampshire. Mathewson said Citizens had achieved natural growth of about 8 percent in addition to this.
"The franchise continues to improve and we think we will continue to generate a lot of profit there," Mathewson said, adding he expected some further expansion through acquisition.
